8.modern-en: Henry IV is unable to sleep at the Westminster palace and reflects in the great 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown' soliloquy.

13.modern-en: Henry IV is brought into the Jerusalem Chamber, exhausted, and lies down to rest beside the crown.

14.modern-en: Henry IV wakes, finds the crown taken from his pillow, summons Hal, and is reconciled to him in their long deathbed exchange.

5.modern-en: Hal walks the London street with Poins, joking about his small-beer habits and his father's illness.

14.modern-en: Hal sits by his sleeping father, believes him dead, takes up the crown to try its weight, and is rebuked by the king who has only fainted.

16.modern-en: Hal, now Henry V, walks into the council chamber and embraces the Lord Chief Justice instead of dismissing him.

18.modern-en: Hal as king is mentioned in the brief street scenes as the new ruler whose first moves have astonished the court.

19.modern-en: Hal, in his coronation procession, meets Falstaff at the abbey gate and dismisses him with 'I know thee not, old man.'

epithet.en: Hal's old companion, a fat knight in mountain decline

2.modern-en: Falstaff is in the London street with his Page asking after his doctor's report on his urine, and is intercepted by the Lord Chief Justice.

4.modern-en: Falstaff dodges Mistress Quickly's attempt to have him arrested for debt, with help from his page and the Lord Chief Justice's grudging tolerance.

5.modern-en: Falstaff is referred to in Hal's banter with Poins as the man whose tavern Hal is too sad to visit just now.

7.modern-en: Falstaff dines at the Boar's Head with Doll Tearsheet and Mistress Quickly, picks a quarrel with Pistol, and is summoned to the court for the wars.

9.modern-en: Falstaff arrives in Gloucestershire to recruit, fleeces Justice Shallow over reminiscences, and impresses old Feeble, Mouldy, Bullcalf, and Shadow.

11.modern-en: Falstaff is at Gaultree Forest collecting his command and contributing nothing.

13.modern-en: Falstaff catches the rebel Coleville and accepts his surrender as if it had been a great deed of arms.

15.modern-en: Falstaff settles in at Justice Shallow's house in Gloucestershire and borrows a thousand pounds against his coming influence at court.

17.modern-en: Falstaff hears at Shallow's orchard that Hal is now king, calls for his horse, and rides at speed for London certain his hour is at hand.

19.modern-en: Falstaff stands at the coronation street, calls out to Hal as the procession passes, and is rejected in front of the city.

epithet.en: Hal's younger brother and the king's commander

8.modern-en: Prince John is at his father's Westminster council on the rebellion.

12.modern-en: Prince John meets the Archbishop's army at Gaultree Forest, promises to address every grievance, then arrests the rebels for treason after they have disbanded their men.

14.modern-en: Prince John attends his father at the deathbed and is given the late king's blessing.

16.modern-en: Prince John is at the council when Hal as Henry V re-confirms the Lord Chief Justice.

18.modern-en: Prince John is named among the king's brothers preparing the realm for the new reign and the looming French campaign.

2.modern-en: The Lord Chief Justice intercepts Falstaff in the street and tries unsuccessfully to remind him of his disgrace.

4.modern-en: The Lord Chief Justice mediates Mistress Quickly's debt suit against Falstaff and is once more outmanoeuvred.

14.modern-en: The Lord Chief Justice appears at the council on the day of the king's death, expecting to be dismissed by the new king.

16.modern-en: The Lord Chief Justice is embraced by Hal as the new Henry V and confirmed in his post.

18.modern-en: The Lord Chief Justice escorts the new king's brothers to the coronation.

epithet.en: Hotspur's father, the rebellion's reluctant leader

1.modern-en: Northumberland receives confused reports of Shrewsbury and, in the end, the news that his son Hotspur is dead.

6.modern-en: Northumberland is dissuaded by his wife and Hotspur's widow from joining the new rebellion and flees instead to Scotland.

3.modern-en: The Archbishop of York gathers the rebel leaders at his palace to plan a new revolt against Henry IV.

10.modern-en: The Archbishop conducts the conference at Gaultree Forest with his demands written out for the king's commander.

11.modern-en: The Archbishop continues the parley as Prince John approaches with the king's army.

12.modern-en: The Archbishop accepts Prince John's terms, dismisses the rebel army, and is at once arrested for treason.

epithet.en: Hostess of the Boar's Head tavern in Eastcheap

4.modern-en: Mistress Quickly tries to have Falstaff arrested for the debts he owes her, and is talked round by him into another loan.

7.modern-en: Mistress Quickly presides over the Boar's Head dinner with Falstaff, Doll Tearsheet, and Pistol.
Doll Tearsheet quarrels with Falstaff at supper, drives Pistol from the room, and sits on Falstaff's knee for the rest of the meal.

18.modern-en: Doll Tearsheet is reported, in passing, as having been carted off to prison along with Mistress Quickly.

7.modern-en: Pistol intrudes on Falstaff's dinner with Doll and is driven out by force after picking a quarrel.

17.modern-en: Pistol arrives at Shallow's orchard with the news that Henry IV is dead and Hal is king.

19.modern-en: Pistol is at Falstaff's side in the coronation street and is dismissed with the rest.

epithet.en: A country justice of the peace in Gloucestershire

9.modern-en: Justice Shallow receives Falstaff and parades his country recruits — Mouldy, Shadow, Wart, Feeble, and Bullcalf — for the king's wars.

15.modern-en: Justice Shallow welcomes Falstaff to his Gloucestershire house and reminisces about their student carousing fifty years before.

17.modern-en: Justice Shallow sits with Falstaff in his orchard eating pippins as Pistol arrives with the news of the king's death.

19.modern-en: Justice Shallow is at Falstaff's side at the coronation procession and is dismissed with him.
